newsitem.title: THAILAND: Alphatec limit down on revamp doubts.
newsitem.headline: Alphatec limit down on revamp doubts.

text.p: Shares of Thailand's component and computer giant Alphatec Electronics Plc continued their recent slide falling the 10 percent daily limit on Monday.
The stock dropped 11 baht to 100 during the afternoon session on the Thai stock exchange.

The shares have dropped their limit over the last four trading days as investors on concerns about the viability of the firm's share restructuring plans and its short-term liquidity situation, brokers said.
Company sources said the firm's situation would be helped by a bridging loan deal to be signed later this week with domestic financial institutions.
The loan size and terms were not disclosed.
Some fund managers were inquiring whether rumours that the firm faced liquidity problem were true, analysts said.
The company said it planned an analysts' meeting soon to clarify the situation, but declined to name a date. A fund manager said an official announcement can be expected on Wednesday.

Brokers said moves by the firm to raise funds through a launch of American Depository Receipts to raise funds and issue new shares to help finance the construction of SubMicron's new wafer fabrication plant, threatened Alphatec's profits and increased risks.

Analysts said SubMicron, which hopes to become Thailand's first wafer fabrication foundry, is due to post losses of around 3.2 billion baht in the next two years as depreciation charges against its new plant will be high.

Alphatec's profitability would be hit by its decision to become the major shareholder in the firm, they added. A portion of funds raised from Alphatec's 319 million baht capital increase will be used to purchase a 46.87 percent stake in SubMicron, Alphatec told the Stock Exchange of Thailand two weeks ago.
"In the long term it may be good but the problems will be over the next one or two years and that is really the focus most people have with this stock," said an electronics analyst.
The stock, which fell to a year low of 158 baht days after news of the share issue was made public on March 14, has fallen a further 58 baht in the past four trading days.
